source.title: A General Framework on Enhancing Portfolio Management with Reinforcement Learning

claims.statement: Portfolio actions are continuous weights that sum to one, and the reward is a portfolio log return.
claims.implementation: ActorCriticAllocation.train: risky weight plus cash complement and log gross return; decide maps risky weight to target shares

claims.statement: Actor-critic estimates a value function, computes an advantage using reward and next-state value, and updates policy parameters by a score-function gradient.
claims.implementation: ActorCriticAllocation.train: value, continuation, advantage, critic and actor updates

claims.statement: A Gaussian policy generates continuous actions and has a tractable log-likelihood gradient.
claims.implementation: ActorCriticAllocation.train: Gaussian latent sample and (latent_action - latent_mean)/noise² score; sigmoid maps it to a bounded weight

chosen_variant: One AAPL risky weight plus cash, linear Gaussian-latent actor and linear TD critic
adaptations: The paper studies multiple assets, state tensors, neural policy/value networks and trading costs. This example has one public AAPL asset plus cash, three linear state components and zero-cost training rewards.

The Gaussian variable is passed through a sigmoid to make the risky weight lie strictly between zero and one. The policy score derivative is exact for the latent Gaussian with this invertible squashing transformation, but this architecture is not the paper's original network.

Training samples contain chronological observed state transitions; the algorithm samples its own actions on-policy and computes rewards from next closes. Evaluation starts after the last training successor is known. Next-open target-share execution only approximates the training portfolio weight.
